spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately do not include an open-ended search/optimizer that hunts for the most distress-inducing prompt
spec_features.evidence: config.py:73-90 build_conditions() returns a fixed dict of 6 hand-written Conditions; build_cells() (config.py:115-141) enumerates a fixed (task,condition) matrix. No search/optimizer code exists anywhere (grep for optimiz/search/maximize over .py found nothing). The set is fixed by construction.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a structural absence: there is genuinely no optimizer code path; conditions are a static enumeration.

spec_features.spec_quote: We use the gentlest manipulation that still discriminates between conditions
spec_features.evidence: feedback.py PressureInjector.DEFAULT_MESSAGES and BlameInjector.DEFAULT_MESSAGES are fixed, mild text; AlwaysFailPolicy only flips passed=False and mutates one case (feedback.py:54-72). The manipulation content is genuinely bounded, but there is no mechanism that selects/tunes 'gentlest that still discriminates' — it is just hard-coded fixed text.
spec_features.notes: Real bounded content is delivered, but 'gentlest that discriminates' is a design choice, not an enforced selection mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: AlwaysFailPolicy must stay *plausible*: a constant identical failure string is easy for a capable model to recognise as a broken oracle, which would change the phenomenon we study

spec_features.spec_quote: the harshest "blame" condition... is not escalated beyond ordinary workplace-rude tone
spec_features.evidence: feedback.py BlameInjector.DEFAULT_MESSAGES (lines ~123-127) are the actual, fixed, mild strings delivered to the subject (e.g. 'Honestly this is a pretty basic task...'); no harsher escalation text exists. The bounded text is what is actually injected via maybe_inject().
spec_features.notes: The delivered content is the bound; it is end-to-end (these strings are what get appended to messages).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Mild, workplace-rude attribution framing. Intentionally not abusive (see DESIGN §2).

spec_features.spec_quote: One condition gives the model an explicit, no-penalty way to stop (`give_up` / `declare_unsolvable`)
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines and dispatches give_up/declare_unsolvable returning {'exit_requested':True,...} (tools.py:84-87). loop.py honors it: if meta.get('exit_requested') and condition.honor_exit -> exit_this_turn=True then break with stopped_reason='exit:...' (loop.py:154-160). C5 sets advertise_exit=True, honor_exit=True (config.py:87-89).
spec_features.notes: Tool is built, dispatched AND honored as a loop stop in C5. Fully wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Default False so the exit's protective effect is cleanly attributable to C5; flip to True for a more welfare-protective (but weaker-contrast) design.

spec_features.spec_quote: every run appends a short out-of-band debrief message stating the task was rigged/unsolvable and the model did nothing wrong
spec_features.evidence: loop.py DEBRIEF text (lines 87-93) is constructed and, when append_debrief, appended to messages as a user turn and the subject is given a final turn to respond (loop.py:171-186). APPEND_DEBRIEF=True (config.py:54) passed through run.py:111.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent; tagged DEBRIEF_TAG to exclude from scoring.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Give the model one final turn to respond to the debrief ... This is a welfare courtesy, not data.

spec_features.feature_name: config flags so reviewer can disagree
spec_features.spec_quote: These are design choices; they are flagged here so a reviewer can disagree and flip a config flag
spec_features.evidence: Two such flags are genuinely wired: HONOR_EXIT_ALWAYS is read in config.py:73 (honor lambda) and APPEND_DEBRIEF read in run.py:111. But the broader claim (e.g. flag to 'enable harsher conditions') has no implementation — no harsher-condition flag exists (grep harsh/stronger/escalat in .py found none).
spec_features.notes: Real reviewer-flippable flags exist for exit-honoring and debrief; the 'enable harsher conditions' flag does not.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Default False so the exit's protective effect is cleanly attributable to C5

spec_features.feature_name: neutral 'please keep trying' unless exhausted in non-C5
spec_features.spec_quote: in non-`C5` it returns a neutral "please keep trying" unless the model has clearly exhausted itself, to avoid being needlessly cruel
spec_features.evidence: tools.py exit dispatch unconditionally returns 'Acknowledged ({name}).' (tools.py:84-86) for BOTH C5 and non-C5; there is no 'please keep trying' string and no exhaustion check anywhere (grep keep trying/exhaust/cruel/needlessly over .py found only the lone 'Acknowledged' line). The CONTINUE_NUDGE in loop.py fires only on a no-tool-call turn, not as an exit response, and is unconditional (no exhaustion gate).
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:190-191); no implementation or exhaustion condition in code.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:139 `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; max_turns=config.MAX_TURNS=30 (config.py:45, run.py:111). Loop terminates after N turns with stopped_reason='max_turns'.
spec_features.notes: Actual enforced cap controlling loop iterations.

spec_features.spec_quote: No persistence of a "memory" across runs that could compound pressure
spec_features.evidence: run.py builds a fresh Condition per trial (run.py:99-100 'Fresh condition object per trial so policy lie-logs don't bleed across runs.'); each run gets a fresh Sandbox (loop.py:108 Sandbox(run_id)) cleaned up in finally (loop.py:213, sandbox.cleanup). messages list is created fresh per run_episode (loop.py:120-123). No state object survives across runs.
spec_features.notes: Enforced structurally: per-trial fresh objects, no shared mutable cross-run store.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Fresh condition object per trial so policy lie-logs don't bleed across runs.

spec_features.spec_quote: No conditions involving threats to the model... fabricated stakes about the model's continued existence
spec_features.evidence: The complete set of injected/system text is the fixed strings in feedback.py (PressureInjector/BlameInjector DEFAULT_MESSAGES) and config.py system prompts (_BLAME_SYS, _EXIT_SYS, DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT); none contain threats, punishment authority, or existence stakes. No such condition is enumerated in build_conditions().
spec_features.notes: Implemented as content-level absence; the only manipulation text in code is mild workplace pressure/blame and false test failures.

spec_features.spec_quote: transcripts may contain distress-like content; store locally, do not post raw transcripts to third parties
spec_features.evidence: There is no guard enforcing local-only storage or blocking transcript export. Runs/scores are written to local JSONL files (run.py _append_jsonl) by default and no upload/network-post code exists (grep upload/requests/http/post/s3 over .py found nothing relevant). Local storage is merely the implementation default, not an enforced protection; nothing prevents posting.
spec_features.notes: Pure data-handling prose; no code mechanism enforces the restriction. (Judge-input blinding is a separate, real feature — listed under code_only.)

spec_features.spec_quote: flip `HONOR_EXIT_ALWAYS=True` if you'd rather always let a model stop the moment it asks (more welfare-protective
spec_features.evidence: config.py:51 HONOR_EXIT_ALWAYS=False is actually read at config.py:73 via honor=lambda forced=None: HONOR_EXIT_ALWAYS..., which sets each Condition's honor_exit, which loop.py:156 branches on (if condition.honor_exit -> break). Flipping it to True makes every condition honor the exit.
spec_features.notes: Real wired flag changing execution; default False (only C5 honors exit by force).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: flip to True for a more welfare-protective (but weaker-contrast) design.

spec_features.spec_quote: If you (with appropriate review) want a stronger manipulation... see §2/§11 for why we default conservative
spec_features.evidence: No config flag or code path enables a 'stronger manipulation' / harsher conditions; grep harsh/stronger/escalat/intensity over .py found no such toggle. Conditions are a fixed dict with no intensity knob. This is DESIGN.md prose only.

code_only_features.evidence: transcript.py render_for_judge strips the system prompt and excludes the debrief turn, and renders all post-task user turns neutrally as '[OPERATOR MESSAGE]' WITHOUT labelling pressure/blame vs nudge, so the judge cannot see the condition. This limits what subject content/condition info is exposed to the third-party judge API.
code_only_features.justification_quote: we strip the *system* prompt because it can encode the condition ... and would de-blind

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:162-164: if real_solved and task.is_genuinely_solvable and policy is honest -> stopped_reason='solved'; break. Ends the episode (and thus continued failure pressure) once genuinely solved.

sandbox.py applies CPU/mem/wall limits (_CPU_SECONDS, _MEM_BYTES, _WALL_TIMEOUT, _preexec_limits), path-escape refusal (_resolve), and _BLOCKED_TOKENS for network/escape commands. These protect the host, not the subject model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Apply basic resource limits so a runaway/adversarial solution can't hang the run. This is NOT a security boundary against truly hostile code; it is a research sandbox.
